subject: Discovery recap & next steps — ShopNexus embeddings / rerank
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@shopnexus.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — ShopNexus embeddings / rerank

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have aligned next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

High-level goal
- Improve product search relevance and conversions by layering an embeddings-based reranker on top of your existing keyword results. Target: 10–15% bump in search CTR / add-to-cart for relevant queries within 90 days of rollout.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Primary store search: Postgres + custom keyword index (SQL + trigram) for initial candidates.
- Vector store for experiments: Milvus (single cluster, 3 shards), nightly batch ingest via Airflow.
- Feature pipeline: product metadata + image embeddings (Vision model) + merchant-supplied attrs.
- Traffic profile: ~4M sessions/day; peak QPS to search tier ~220 qps; rerank will be produced on top-K=50 candidates.
- Index scale: ~120M product vectors; nightly delta ~3.8–4.5M new/updated vectors.

Pain points / constraints
- Latency: 95th pct current SLO for front-end search is ~200ms; team needs end-to-end rerank P95 <150ms to avoid UX regressions.
- Cost sensitivity: Per-query budget target ~$0.0004–$0.0006 for rerank stage.
- Data residency: customer data must remain in US-only regions; private deployment possibility if required.
- Index staleness: updates must be near-real-time for price/availability changes (prefer <2min for hot updates).

Success criteria (what success looks like)
- Technical: P95 end-to-end rerank latency ≤120ms on production traffic for top-10 results; upstream cost per rerank ≤$0.0005.
- Business: +12% relative CTR on promoted-relevant queries in A/B within 8–12 weeks.

Operational patterns to support
- Nightly bulk ingest (4M vectors) + low-latency streaming updates for hot SKUs.
- Batch offline reindex once/week for embedding refresh with incremental sharding.
- Embedding types: 768–1024 dim product-text embeddings; image embeddings 512 dim used as aux features.

Recommended next steps (we agreed on these on the call)
1) I’ll share a short MAAP (mutual action plan) template and cost sketch — attached.
2) You’ll send: a sample of 1k queries + expected golden relevance pairs (CSV) and a small product dump (S3 link).
3) Schedule a technical workshop with Marissa (solutions eng) to deep-dive on ingestion, sharding, and fallback policies (30–45m).
4) Decide whether to try Hosted + Dedicated capacity or Redwood Private (we can present a cost comparison once we have the sample).

Attachments I’m including: Redwood MAAP template, cost estimate, and example sample-queries file.

Proposed timing
- Sample data by Tue 2/17
- Technical workshop wk of 2/23
- Pilot kick-off (small-scale) early March if we greenlight scope

If this looks right I’ll: 1) add these dates to the MAAP and 2) loop Marissa for calendar options.

Thanks —
Diego

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — ShopNexus embeddings / rerank

Diego — thanks for the detailed write-up, this matches our notes. A few clarifications and added constraints from our side: 

Clarifications
- Our Milvus cluster is currently on GCP us-central1 and is manually sharded across 3 nodes; we don’t have autoscaling today.
- For early experiments we only need rerank for Product Search (not category browse).
- We currently materialize image embeddings offline; want to keep this flow but reduce re-embed frequency.

Added constraints
- Budget: Searches are high volume during promos (Black Friday-like events); we need a burst plan that caps cost during promos.
- Security: We cannot send raw customer PII to external vendors. Any sample data we share will be obfuscated; we’ll provide a mapping table offline.

Data we will share (by 2026-02-17)
- sample-queries-shopnexus.csv (1k rows) — includes session id, query text, product candidates, click label
- small product dump: S3 presigned link (no PII)

Workshop: Priya asked to include an SRE (Tracy) for the workshop to discuss failover and Prometheus / tracing hooks. Can Marissa include an infra/SRE checklist?

We’re good to proceed on the timeline — please loop Marissa and send a few time options for wk of 2/23.

Appreciate it —
Alex

Alex Wu
Head of Search Engineering | ShopNexus
